visual_appeal: Reduce the ElvUI title region from roughly 48 px to 32 px. Its tall, streaked black surface currently consumes attention without adding useful hierarchy.

Use a consistent surface ladder: #100D09 window background, #19140E cards, #241D14 selected or elevated surfaces, and #51412B internal borders. Keep the authentic WC3 outer frame, but reduce competing internal gold rules.

Make buttons consistently 24 px high with 12 px horizontal padding. The tiny View details button, blue footer controls and gold action controls currently look assembled from different component families.
play_next_clarity: Keep the hero name dominant, but increase PLAY NEXT from its tiny caption treatment to 13 px bold and give it 6 px separation from the name.

Replace the hero instruction with two explicitly ordered clauses: First: hearth Le Jette to an inn. Then: play Le Dette. Preserve class-coloured names within that instruction rather than rendering the entire sentence gold.
Restore useful magnitude to NOW PLAYING: replace None used yet with ~1 double-XP kill left when applicable. None used yet describes consumption, not whether this character is safe to play.
Change View details to Character details. The primary decision is already visible; the button should clearly describe its secondary destination.
state_colours: Keep all four state hues, but define one shared token per state for bars, rails, legend dots and chips. The default orange-brown chips currently blend into the brown row backgrounds; use #F0A43A for their border and a near-black fill.

The rested-XP-used-up toast has a green rail and green supporting text. Use the exhausted character's state for the rail, then reserve green for a separate recommendation line such as Le Dette is fully rested.

Give timeline lanes with fill dates beyond 48 hours a clear right-pointing continuation cap and label such as Full 2 Dec · beyond view. Their almost complete horizontal bars otherwise resemble progress toward completion within the visible window.
character_identity: Retain the settled portrait and badge rules, but enlarge roster badges to 16 px and give them a 1 px dark separation ring. The small grayscale race/gender badges are difficult to distinguish at the supplied scale.

In the saved-look card, remove the duplicate Last seen as a level 11 Tauren Druid block. Put Level 11 Tauren Druid · Seen 23h ago directly under the name and use the reclaimed space for a better-balanced portrait composition.

Move the saved portrait approximately 28 px left and align its vertical centre with the speech area. The current card leaves a large central void while pressing the portrait and class badge toward the right edge.
default_theme: Darken the default roster fills from the current medium brown to approximately #251D13, with alternating rows no more than 5% lighter. The large brown slab is heavier than the attractive landscape hero.
Reduce the portrait's gold outer ring to 2 px and retain a separate 1 px state-colour ring. The current luminous double frame competes with the character name.
Use the same restrained gold button treatment for Compact, account selection and Character details, with distinct hover and pressed states rather than several unrelated brown fills.
elvui_wc3_fit: Bring the options page beside the supplied real Options reference: replace the opaque medium-gray/brown field with a near-black brown content panel, use #171717 section headers, and retain yellow for settings labels rather than every explanatory paragraph.

Match the reference's squared, compact control language: 1 px dark outlines, blue secondary buttons and the skin's existing close-button proportions. Avoid introducing a separate decorative button system inside ElvUI mode.

Standardize alert surfaces through the loaded skin. The logout banner is textured and framed, the Esc card is a flat gray rectangle, and the toast is wood-textured; these should share the same background, border and inset treatment.
alerts_ux: Expose Reset on every move placeholder. In the supplied move-mode scene it is clearly visible on Toasts but not on Logout warning or Esc menu card. Give each a consistent 56 × 20 px top-right Reset control.
Reserve a 24 px drag header on each placeholder and show attachment state beneath it. For the Esc card use Attached to Esc menu or Custom position, with Reset reattaches as explicit helper copy.
Increase close-button hit areas to at least 24 × 24 px, while retaining the small WC3 visual glyph. Keep them 6 px inside the frame rather than tight against text or borders.
Replace Cancel the logout first with Cancel logout, then hearth to an inn. It is a clearer recovery instruction and avoids the awkward current phrasing.
readability: Raise roster metadata, timing text and footer text to at least 13 px at native scale; use 14 px for primary row names. Do not rely on the simulator's font-width difference to solve the dense vertical hierarchy.
Use #E8DDC6 for normal information and #B8AD98 for secondary information. Reserve bright gold for headings and actionable emphasis instead of rendering nearly the entire options page yellow.
Display the warning slider's current value as a persistent 10% label above its thumb or beside its heading. The visible 5% and 50% endpoints are not enough for precise adjustment.
Add 3–4 px between roster bars and their timing labels. The text currently feels tucked against the bars, especially when exact timestamps appear.
layout_polish: Give the footer a fixed grid: account-link controls on the left, account filter in the middle, visibility checkbox on the right. Keep the sync status to one line or place it below the link control in a deliberately taller footer.

Align roster names, metadata baselines, bar starts and state-chip edges to shared columns. Keep at least 16 px between the bar column and state chips rather than letting the timing strings visually bridge both.

Reorganize options into Appearance, Accounts, Notifications and Alerts with 16 px between sections. Move the long licensing and transport explanation into a small About subsection rather than a dense yellow block at the bottom.
Give timeline midnight transitions explicit day/date labels above the grid. Replace the isolated Wed heading with Wed 25 Nov or the actual fixture date, while keeping six-hour ticks beneath it.
delight: Keep the short character-specific speech, but integrate the bubble more deliberately: use 10 px internal padding, a consistent tail and no collision with metadata. The hero's current narrow outlined strip feels more like a tooltip fragment than a character speaking.
Make the saved-look card's sleeping treatment intentional: place a subtle three-glyph sleep cluster near the portrait, not isolated against the upper-right background.

Add a restrained 250 ms gold highlight when a different character becomes PLAY NEXT, disabled by Reduce motion. Avoid a full-card sweep; the reward should reinforce the recommendation without interrupting scanning.

overall_notes: A meaningful improvement over the baseline: the next character is obvious, the roster is less truncated, and the new timeline and movable notifications have real utility. This is not yet a 9-level approval. The remaining problems are systemic rather than decorative nits: inconsistent alert surfaces, an options page that does not sit convincingly beside the supplied real skin, cramped secondary typography, and unfinished spacing and control hierarchy. The default hero is the strongest visual surface; carry that discipline into the footer, options and notifications. No deduction for simulator model placeholders, the established state palette, class-coloured names or the settled portrait fallback rules.
